A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ScienceAgentBench and retain the same 102-task benchmark. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments with five LLMs and three frameworks, repeated-run results in Appendix D, and human evaluations of 102 generated programs.

after.justification: v3 retains these experiments and adds o1 evaluations, an analysis of 100 error trajectories, and qualitative reasoning case studies.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction procedures, contamination safeguards, and three evaluated frameworks remain unchanged. Adding o1 as an evaluated model and discussing its reasoning do not introduce a proposed algorithm or modify the existing self-debug procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 102 tasks from 44 publications across four disciplines. Task examples and source lists are retained. The added evaluations and case studies do not introduce a new dataset, domain, or task requirement.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds OpenAI o1-preview under direct prompting and self-debug, with and without expert knowledge. The original five models and their framework comparisons remain. o1 is explicitly excluded from OpenHands because of compatibility limitations.

E3.justification: v3 adds o1 using default hyperparameters and an error-analysis sample of 50 failed trajectories per framework. It also revises the documented rubric examples: Clintox increases from 75 to 80 points and expands transformation requirements; the geographical rubric changes from 100 to 90 points through reweighting and removal of a formatting item (G.2/G.4 to H.2/H.4). These revisions do not establish that existing evaluations were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends the existing illustrative cases with a systematic analysis of 100 failures, quantifying semantic errors, environment-configuration failures, and OpenHands editing difficulties (Appendix E.2). Appendix F.3 additionally examines o1 reasoning summaries for two tasks. These add comparative failure analysis and a new investigation of planning behavior; the original analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix D.2 newly discloses five independent runs of the Clintox reference program supporting the 0.77 ROC-AUC threshold. This is newly reported run information, not evidence of an increased run count. The existing three-run evaluation and mean/standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged; additional o1 rows follow the same practice.

E6.justification: All original Table 3 scores and appendix means/standard deviations are retained. New o1 results include self-debug success rates of 42.2% without knowledge and 41.2% with knowledge, plus direct-prompting results and costs. These are additional-model results under different settings, not same-setting gains. v3 also adds quantified failure findings, including semantic errors in 29/50 OpenHands and 30/50 self-debug trajectories.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs. The evaluation definitions remain unchanged; the added threshold rationale and reasoning hypotheses are explanatory and empirical rather than new mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The central contribution and call for task-level assessment before claiming end-to-end scientific automation remain. The abstract adds the claim that o1 reaches 42.2% success through additional inference-time compute at substantially higher cost. The introduction and results qualify its comparability with the original models.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations involving fabricated data, simplified substitute models, environment setup, and inadequate self-verification. It hypothesizes three o1 planning strategies and qualifies comparisons because of different inference settings. The expanded ethics statement specifies task and laboratory-access boundaries, while the original benchmark limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 supplies GPT-4o and Claude snapshot dates in Table 3, identifies the o1 API version and parameter restrictions, and explains that reasoning summaries were obtained through ChatGPT. Appendix D clarifies reference-program preparation and threshold provenance. Existing prompts, validation materials, repository lists, and access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references concerning o1, research-environment setup, scientific-agent safety, and chain-of-thought reasoning. Table 2 changes DiscoveryBench-Real from 'No Code Gen' to 'Code Gen' and explains its indirect evaluation through natural-language hypotheses. The broader related-work discussion remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized abstract edits, an updated publication header, new appendix subsections, and a standalone expanded ethics statement. Future directions move from the conclusion into Appendix A. Most existing prose, section organization, and appendix material remain intact.

P2.justification: The result tables gain shaded o1 rows and explanatory captions; the appendix mean/standard-deviation tables now occupy separate pages. Two boxed reasoning examples are added, and rubric captions are revised. All four original figures retain identical graphical content.

improvement.justification: The added o1 evaluations, systematic failure analysis, and threshold provenance make the benchmark more informative and easier to assess. The gains are bounded: o1 uses different settings, its planning explanations remain qualitative, and the revised rubric examples are not accompanied by a documented update to the unchanged human-evaluation figure. The core benchmark and original evidence remain intact.
